Title 2: Define churn/retention target and eligibility rules
Description: Confirm the churn/retention definition, eligible population, exclusions and applicable business rules for modelling.

Title 2: Define as-of date, feature window and outcome window
Description: Document the observation date, historical feature period and future outcome period used to create features and labels.

Title 2: Identify required source fields and approved views
Description: Confirm the Databricks source tables/views and fields required to build the churn modelling dataset.
Join required source datasets, standardise fields and apply agreed preparation and business-rule logic.
Create the modelling dataset at one row per account_id per as_of_date with lower-level records aggregated to account level.

Title 2: Validate modelling dataset grain and record counts
Description: Check uniqueness, row counts, account coverage and expected population after dataset creation.
Create account tenure, lifecycle and relevant time-based features available as of the observation date.
Create approved product and account attributes required for churn modelling and segmentation.

Create account-level engagement features from approved interaction and engagement data sources.
Create trend/change features that capture changes in customer behaviour over agreed historical periods.

Apply deterministic missing-value handling appropriate to each feature and document the treatment.

Title 1: Story 4.3.3: Validate and Select ML Features

Description: Review feature completeness, ranges, nulls and unexpected values before model development.
Confirm the feature dataset contains no unintended duplicate account_id/as_of_date records.
Confirm no feature uses information occurring after the as_of_date or directly reveals the future target.
Identify features with little or no variation or limited predictive usefulness for potential exclusion.
Select the modelling feature set based on quality, business relevance and modelling suitability.
Review identified features and business interpretation with the Business SME and record feedback/sign-off.

Title 2: Document feature and dataset version traceability
Description: Record feature definitions and dataset versions so training and future scoring logic can be reproduced.

Title 1: Story 4.4.1: Prepare Training and Validation Datasets

Description: Prepare numeric and categorical inputs in the format required by the candidate model pipelines.

Title 2: Create temporal train, validation and test split
Description: Split historical observations by time so model development and evaluation reflect future scoring behaviour.
Check churn/non-churn distribution across train, validation and test datasets for material differences.

Title 2: Validate training and test dataset consistency
Description: Confirm feature schema, transformations and data types are consistent across modelling datasets.

Title 1: Story 4.4.2: Develop and Tune Candidate ML Models

Description: Train a simple baseline model to provide a minimum benchmark for candidate model performance.
Train and track a Logistic Regression candidate using the approved training dataset.
Train and track a Decision Tree candidate using consistent feature and evaluation logic.
Train and track a Random Forest candidate using consistent feature and evaluation logic.

Title 2: Develop XGBoost or alternative candidate model
Description: Train XGBoost or an agreed alternative candidate model subject to runtime and library availability.
Tune selected candidate-model parameters to improve validated performance; execute only if agreed as required.
Log model parameters, metrics, artifacts and runs in MLflow for reproducibility and comparison.

Title 1: Story 4.4.3: Evaluate and Select Final Churn Model

Description: Compare candidate models using ROC-AUC and PR-AUC, with emphasis on performance for the churn class.
Compare precision, recall and F1 at relevant classification thresholds.
Assess prediction errors and model lift to understand practical churn-identification performance.
Check whether predicted churn probabilities are suitably calibrated for risk scoring and business use.
Compare candidate models consistently across technical metrics, stability and operational considerations.
Select the preferred model based on agreed technical and business criteria.
Record why the selected model was preferred and note key trade-offs versus alternative candidates.

Description: Produce model-level feature importance to identify the strongest overall churn drivers.
Generate account-level explanations showing the main factors influencing each churn-risk prediction.
Transform explainability outputs into interpretable churn/risk-driver fields for downstream consumption.
Define churn-risk bands from predicted probabilities and validate their population and observed behaviour.

Title 2: Review model results and drivers with Business SME
Description: Review model performance, risk bands and key drivers with the Business SME and capture feedback/sign-off.

Description: Monitor important model inputs for material distribution changes relative to the approved reference data.
